system_note: Claim RM_04 (readmit admit 06/13/2026) paired to index claim MR_04 (discharged 05/23/2026); gap_days = 21, which is within Lake Ontario Health Cooperative's 30-day review window (Policy Documents/Readmission/Payer Guidelines/Lake Ontario Health Cooperative - Readmission Review Guideline.docx, Review Window:, position 4: "30 days from prior discharge"). The readmission principal diagnosis is T84.612A (infection/inflammatory reaction due to internal fixation device of left femur). The facility discharge summary documents that the patient "re-presented to the ED 7 days after returning home from the IRF with infection and inflammatory reaction due to internal fixation device, left femur (T84.612A); osteomyelitis (M86.262); E. coli sepsis (A41.51) - a direct infectious complication of the orthopedic hardware placed during the index trauma admission." (DISCHARGE SUMMARY, DISCHARGE SUMMARY, pp. 124-125). Under the Lake Ontario guideline, a readmission that is "due to a new infection, bleeding event, or other complication arising from care provided during the prior stay" qualifies as a Finding under the 'infection or complication of care' criterion (Policy Documents/Readmission/Payer Guidelines/Lake Ontario Health Cooperative - Readmission Review Guideline.docx, position 13: "Does the documentation support: The readmission is due to a new infection, bleeding event, or other complication arising from care provided during the prior stay..."). I reviewed the guideline exclusions list (Policy Documents/Readmission/Payer Guidelines/Lake Ontario Health Cooperative - Readmission Review Guideline.docx, position 21: "Does the readmission meet any of the following exclusions? Direct transfers... Readmissions that were scheduled... Admissions to a skilled nursing facility... ") - none of those exclusions apply to this readmission (the readmission was an acute-care hospital admission for hardware infection, later discharged to a SNF). Medical record evidence (culture-proven E. coli peri-implant infection, wound/IMN site findings, hardware removal and ID/ortho co-management, and plan for continued IV antibiotics) directly links the readmission diagnosis to the orthopedic hardware placed during the index MR_04 stay, satisfying the guideline's infection/complication criterion. Determination: Finding - readmission is clinically related to the index admission under the 'infection or complication of care' criterion. Cited documents used: Lake Ontario Health Cooperative Readmission Review Guideline (positions 4, 13, 21) and the RM_04 Discharge Summary (DISCHARGE SUMMARY, pp. 124-125).
rationale_letter: Re: Readmission review of RM_04 (index MR_04) Dear Provider, After review of the medical record and Lake Ontario Health Cooperative's Readmission Review Guideline, this readmission (RM_04, admit 06/13/2026) has been determined to be clinically related to the prior index admission (MR_04, discharged 05/23/2026) and therefore is a Finding under the payer's policy. The readmission occurred within the payer's 30-day review window (Lake Ontario Health Cooperative guideline: "30 days from prior discharge"). Basis for Determination: - Policy: Lake Ontario Health Cooperative's guideline states that a readmission qualifies as a Finding when it is "due to a new infection, bleeding event, or other complication arising from care provided during the prior stay." (Policy Documents/Readmission/Payer Guidelines/Lake Ontario Health Cooperative - Readmission Review Guideline.docx, position 13). - Clinical facts: The hospital discharge summary for RM_04 documents that the patient "re-presented to the ED 7 days after returning home from the IRF with infection and inflammatory reaction due to internal fixation device, left femur (T84.612A); osteomyelitis (M86.262); E. coli sepsis (A41.51) - a direct infectious complication of the orthopedic hardware placed during the index trauma admission." (DISCHARGE SUMMARY, DISCHARGE SUMMARY, pp. 124-125). Wound culture isolated E. coli and orthopedic surgery removed the intramedullary nail during the readmission; Infectious Diseases and Orthopedics co-managed care with an extended IV antibiotic plan. - Exclusions: The guideline's exclusions were reviewed and do not apply to this acute-care readmission (Policy Documents/Readmission/Payer Guidelines/Lake Ontario Health Cooperative - Readmission Review Guideline.docx, position 21). Correction/Outcome: Because the readmission is documented and determined to be a direct infectious complication of hardware placed during the index admission, the readmission meets the Lake Ontario Health Cooperative 'infection or complication of care' criterion and is being adjudicated as a Finding under the payer's readmission review policy. Please direct any questions or appeals to the payer's medical review contact and include any additional documentation you wish considered. Sincerely, Clinical Review Team Lake Ontario Regional Medical Center
